text:
jordan_acme: Hi, hitting an odd bug with the rerank endpoint. We feed it embeddings we generated in our service and all scores come back as 0.0 or very small negatives. Previously this worked. Any ideas?

emma_support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste the request body you sent (redact keys)? Also which embedding model did you use to create the vectors?

jordan_acme: sure. we use `acme/emb-v3` (internal) to produce 1536-d floats and then call `/v1/rerank` with `model: "redwood-reranker-v1"`. request body snippet: ```json
{"query":"best payment gateway","query_embedding":[0.0012,-0.23,...],"document_embeddings":[[0.0,0.12,...],[...]]}
```

raj_engineer: quick check — are the embeddings normalized? rerank expects the exact dim the model was trained on (1536) and typically un-normalized floats in float32 range. if you accidentally quantized to int8 or sent base64 we might misinterpret.

jordan_acme: we convert to float32 and send as arrays. lengths match (1536). Not normalized intentionally. We saw logs showing `score: -0.0000` for many docs. Also noticed a billing spike because our app retried requests when scores were weird.

emma_support: hmm. Can you share a minimal reproducible curl (no keys) and one exact vector for query+doc? Even a short toy that reproduces helps.

jordan_acme: minimal: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-reranker-v1","query":"x","query_embedding":[0.001,0.002,...1536 items...],"document_embeddings":[{"id":"d1","embedding":[0.0009,0.0021,...]}]}'
```

olivia_ml: can you confirm the embedding model name used to produce your vectors? If the embedding model changed (different family) the dense space will differ and cosine/inner-product will be meaningless — but that usually results in low non-zero scores, not zeros. Also did your pipeline accidentally flip order (doc vs query) or send shape [1536,1] vs [1536]?

jordan_acme: embedding model unchanged. We did a deploy yesterday that swapped a preprocessor library — only change was we started casting to float16 to save memory. Could float16 be the cause?

raj_engineer: yes, float16 can affect values but usually not zero them out. Two quick reproduction checks: 1) send exactly the same vectors you generate to our embeddings endpoint and ask us to verify dims/format, 2) try a small payload with random vectors (all nonzero) to verify rerank scoring logic. Also check for accidental JSON truncation in your client (ellipsis in logs sometimes indicates truncated array).

emma_support: i'm creating an internal repro using your example. Also checking if our rerank API has recently rolled a model variant that changed expected dims or signature. @sre-bot can you confirm if any rerank model rollout happened in the last 24h?

sre-bot: [deploy-bot] No rerank model rollouts in prod in the last 48h. Canary checks green. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

olivia_ml: another likely culprit: mixing embeddings from two different embedding families (e.g., you generate with `acme/emb-v3` but a preprocessing step applied an alignment transform for `acme/emb-v2`). That yields near-orthogonal vectors and extremely small inner products — effectively zero. Did the deploy change how you serialize vectors (little/big endian, base64 vs array)?

jordan_acme: after digging, our new preproc converted arrays to half-precision and then base64-encoded them in our client for transport, but the HTTP layer used `Content-Type: application/json` and sent the base64 string as if it were an array. So our server parsed it as a 1-element string entry then padded/truncated JSON parse -> produced shape mismatch. Looks like our client-side bug.

emma_support: ah that explains it. When the API receives a string instead of an array it attempts to coerce and you can end up with an unexpected shape or sentinel values leading to zeroed scores. Can you confirm the raw JSON we received? I can share a sample sanitized payload.

jordan_acme: yes here's the sanitized request we saw in our request logs: ```json
{"model":"redwood-reranker-v1","query_embedding":"H4sIAAAAA...base64...","document_embeddings":[{"id":"d1","embedding":"H4sIA..."}]}
```

raj_engineer: ok that's a client error — you either need to send arrays or use the embeddings upload API that accepts base64 blobs and specify format. We'll add a clearer error in the server path, but for now fix: send raw arrays of floats (JSON arrays) or call the binary endpoint.

olivia_ml: also recommend verifying dims after decoding: `len(query_embedding) == 1536` and `all(isinstance(x, (int,float)) for x in embedding)`. If you must use float16, expand to float32 before sending (server expects float32 values in JSON arrays).

emma_support: For the billing spike: i flagged a refund ticket — retry storms from clients often cause repeat charges on usage-based flows. i'll open ticket with finance and mark this as escalated for a small credit.

jordan_acme: thanks, will patch the client this morning and redeploy. appreciate the quick triage.

emma_support: closing loop steps for record: 1) root cause: client sent base64/float16 instead of JSON float32 array -> server coerced -> shape/format mismatch -> near-zero scores. 2) short-term: patch client to send arrays or use correct binary endpoint. 3) ops: support flagged billing review. 4) eng: raj to add clearer 400-level error when embedding is non-array.

raj_engineer: will add a schema validation rule and a clear error message: `400 InvalidEmbeddingFormat: expected array of floats (len=1536)`. I'll aim for a small patch today.

jordan_acme: verified fix in dev — rescored fine once arrays sent. thanks all :thumbsup:

emma_support: marking resolved. Reopen if anything else pops up.
